original_interpretation: TSMC said revenue from AI accelerators accounted for a high-teens percentage of its total revenue in 2025.
evidence_found: "Revenue from AI accelerators accounted for high-teens percent of our total revenue in 2025." (TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.5, C.C. Wei prepared remarks)

original_interpretation: In January 2026 TSMC raised its forecast for AI accelerator revenue growth to approach a mid-to-high-fifties percent CAGR over 2024-2029, and overall revenue growth to approach 25% CAGR in US dollar terms.
evidence_found: "Based on our planning framework, we raise our forecast for the revenue growth from AI Accelerators to approach a mid-to-high-fifties % CAGR for the (added by company after the call) five-year period from 2024 to 2029. ... we now expect our overall long-term revenue growth to approach a 25% CAGR, in US dollar terms, for the five-year period starting from 2024." (TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.6)
notes: Passage is on p.6 of the PDF, not p.5 as recorded. Range 55-59 is the researcher's translation of 'mid-to-high-fifties'. Company forecast correctly typed as estimate.

original_interpretation: TSMC's advanced packaging revenue was slightly over 10% of its revenue in 2025, up from about 8% in 2024, and TSMC expected low-teens percent in 2026.
evidence_found: "the revenue contribution last year from advanced packaging is slightly over 10% (corrected by company after the call). It's about 8% in 2024. We expect it to grow faster than the corporate average, and account for low-teens % in 2026." (Wendell Huang, TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.10)
notes: Consistent with the 4Q24 transcript ('over 8%' for 2024). The 4Q25 figure is labelled 'advanced packaging'; the 4Q24 statement was 'advanced packaging and testing'.

original_interpretation: TSMC guided a 2026 capital budget of US$52-56 billion, with 10-20% for advanced packaging, testing, mask making and others.
evidence_found: "In 2026, we expect our capital budget to be between USD52 billion and USD56 billion ... about 10 to 20 percent will be spent for advanced packaging, testing, mask making and others (added by company after the call)." (TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.4). Newer: W.Media, 16 Jul 2026: TSMC "raised its capital budget for 2026 to between US$ 60 billion and US$ 64 billion", with "between 10 and 20 percent for advanced packaging, testing, mask making, and others".
correction: US$52-56bn was the January 2026 guidance. At its 2Q26 call on 16 July 2026 TSMC raised 2026 capital budget guidance to US$60-64bn (allocation split unchanged: 70-80% advanced process, about 10% specialty, 10-20% advanced packaging/testing/masks/others). Search results also mention an intermediate April 2026 update (not opened). Superseding claim added.
notes: The January claim is accurate as dated guidance; it is outdated only as the current 2026 guidance. The superseding source is news (tier 3, https://w.media/tsmc-raises-2026-capital-budget-to-us-64-billion-as-hpc-demand-surges/); TSMC's own 2Q26 transcript should be used to upgrade it.

original_interpretation: TSMC's chairman said in January 2026 that capacity for AI demand was 'very tight' and that closing the gap would take hard work in 2026 and 2027.
evidence_found: "And so, both in Taiwan and in Arizona, we speeded up our capacity expansion to meet the AI demand. I can always say one word. The capacity is very tight. We work very hard to narrow the gap so far. Probably this year, next year, we have to work extremely hard to narrow the gap." (C.C. Wei, TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.9)

original_interpretation: TSMC's chairman reported that a cloud-provider customer told him TSMC silicon, not power supply, was the binding bottleneck for its AI data centres, because it had planned power 5-6 years earlier.
evidence_found: "I use one of my customers' customers' answer. I asked the same question. They told me that they planned this one, 5-6 years ago already. So, as I said, those cloud service providers are smart ... So, they say that they work on the power supply 5-6 years ago. So, today, their message to me is - silicon from TSMC is a bottleneck, and asked me not to pay attention to all others, because they have to solve the silicon bottleneck first." (C.C. Wei, TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026), p.10)
correction: The speaker was 'one of my customers' customers' (a cloud service provider buying from TSMC's customers), not a TSMC customer. 'Binding bottleneck' is the researcher's gloss of 'silicon from TSMC is a bottleneck ... have to solve the silicon bottleneck first'.
notes: Anecdote relayed by the CEO about a single unnamed CSP; reported_claim typing is correct.

original_interpretation: TSMC said cloud service providers (its customers' customers) were reaching out to TSMC directly to request capacity, and that engagement lead time with customers is at least two to three years.
evidence_found: "our customers' customer, who are mainly the cloud service providers, are also providing strong signals and reaching out directly to request the capacity to support their business." (p.5); "as process technology complexity increases, the engagement lead time with customers is now at least two to three years in advance." (p.6) (TSMC 4Q25 transcript (LSEG edited, event 15 Jan 2026))
notes: Lead-time passage is on p.6, not p.5.

original_interpretation: TSMC defines 'AI accelerators' revenue as revenue from AI GPUs, AI ASICs and HBM controllers used for AI training and inference in the data centre.
evidence_found: "Revenue from AI accelerators, which we now define as AI GPU, AI ASIC, and HBM controller for AI training and inference in the data center, accounted for close to mid-teens percent our total revenue in 2024." (TSMC 4Q24 transcript (Refinitiv edited, event 16 Jan 2025), p.5, C.C. Wei prepared remarks)
notes: Definition introduced ('now define') in January 2025; the 4Q25 'high-teens' figure is assumed to use the same definition (not restated in the 4Q25 transcript).

original_interpretation: TSMC said AI accelerators accounted for close to mid-teens percent of its total revenue in 2024, after that revenue more than tripled during 2024.
evidence_found: "accounted for close to mid-teens percent our total revenue in 2024. Even after more than tripling in 2024, we forecast our revenue from AI accelerator to double in 2025" (TSMC 4Q24 transcript (Refinitiv edited, event 16 Jan 2025), p.5)
notes: Confirmed TSMC's own transcript says 'close to mid-teens percent', supporting the researcher's rejection of MarketBeat's 'close to 18%' rendering.

original_interpretation: In January 2025 TSMC forecast AI accelerator revenue to double in 2025 and to grow at approaching a mid-40% CAGR over 2024-2029.
evidence_found: "we forecast our revenue from AI accelerator to double in 2025"; "we now forecast the revenue growth from AI accelerators to approach a mid-40% CAGR for the five-year period starting off the already higher base of 2024." (TSMC 4Q24 transcript (Refinitiv edited, event 16 Jan 2025), p.5; repeated p.18)
notes: Range 43-47 is the researcher's translation of 'mid-40%'.

original_interpretation: Within one year TSMC raised its 2024-2029 AI accelerator revenue CAGR forecast from approaching mid-40% (January 2025) to approaching mid-to-high-fifties % (January 2026).
evidence_found: Both component statements re-found: 4Q24 transcript p.5 'approach a mid-40% CAGR for the five-year period starting off the already higher base of 2024'; 4Q25 transcript p.6 'we raise our forecast ... to approach a mid-to-high-fifties % CAGR for the ... five-year period from 2024 to 2029'.
notes: Inference follows directly from CLM-0776 and CLM-0768; both use a 2024 base and a five-year period.

original_interpretation: In January 2025 TSMC's chairman said CoWoS capacity was all AI-focused and 'very tight' and could not meet customers' needs.
evidence_found: Analyst asked when non-AI applications would adopt CoWoS. C.C. Wei: "Well, yes, today is all AI focused, and we have very tight capacity and cannot even meet customers' need." (TSMC 4Q24 transcript (Refinitiv edited, event 16 Jan 2025), p.14, Q&A)
notes: 'All AI focused' refers to CoWoS, per the question.

original_interpretation: TSMC said advanced packaging and testing accounted for over 8% of its 2024 revenue, with gross margin improving but still below the corporate average.
evidence_found: "advanced packaging and testing accounted for over 8% of revenue last year, and it will account for over 10% this year. In terms of gross margins, it is better. It is better than before, but still below the corporate average." (Wendell Huang, TSMC 4Q24 transcript (Refinitiv edited, event 16 Jan 2025), p.20)

original_interpretation: SK hynix's 2024 revenue was KRW 66.19 trillion with operating profit of KRW 23.47 trillion, a turnaround from an operating loss in 2023; revenue rose 102%.
evidence_found: "Revenues for 2024 at 66.1930 trillion won, operating profit at 23.4673 trillion won, net profit at 19.7969 trillion won"; results table: Revenues 66,193.0, YoY 32,765.7, 102%; Operating profit FY23 -7,730.3, FY24 23,467.3 (KRW bn), "Turn to profit" (SK hynix 4Q24 release as reproduced by StorageNewsletter, 23 Jan 2025)
notes: Source reproduces SK hynix's press release on an industry-press site; SK hynix's own newsroom would be the tier-1 original.

original_interpretation: SK hynix said HBM accounted for over 40% of its total DRAM revenue in the fourth quarter of 2024.
evidence_found: "High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) continued its high growth in fourth quarter marking over 40% of total DRAM revenue" (SK hynix 4Q24 release as reproduced by StorageNewsletter)

original_interpretation: SK hynix's 2025 revenue was KRW 97.15 trillion and operating profit KRW 47.21 trillion (about 49% operating margin), nearly double 2024's operating profit.
evidence_found: "FY2025 revenue of 97.1467 trillion won, operating profit of 47.2063 trillion won" ... "an operating margin of 49%"; "The annual operating profit nearly doubled year-on-year" (SK hynix FY25 release as reproduced by StorageNewsletter, 10 Feb 2026)
notes: 47.2063/23.4673 = 2.01x, consistent with 'nearly doubled'.

original_interpretation: SK hynix said its HBM revenue more than doubled in 2025 and that it was in large-scale production of HBM4 after completing development in September 2025.
evidence_found: "HBM revenue more than doubled year-on-year"; "Having successfully completed the preparation stages to mass produce HBM4 - for the first time in the industry - in September last year, the large-scale production of the next-generation HBM has been underway" (SK hynix FY25 release as reproduced by StorageNewsletter)
correction: The source says SK hynix completed 'the preparation stages to mass produce HBM4' in September 2025, not that it 'completed development'. HBM revenue more than doubling and large-scale next-generation HBM production are supported.

original_interpretation: SK hynix's swing from an operating loss in 2023 to about a 49% operating margin in 2025 (58% in 4Q25) indicates that HBM-led memory makers captured a large share of AI hardware profit by 2025, not only GPU designers.
evidence_found: Numeric basis re-checked: SK hynix FY23 operating profit -7,730.3 KRW bn (SRC-0258 table); FY25 operating margin 49% and 4Q25 operating margin 58% (SRC-0257).
notes: Interpretation; the underlying numbers are supported. 'Captured a large share of AI hardware profit' is a directional reading, not a measured share of an AI profit pool.

original_interpretation: Micron said its HBM revenue grew to nearly US$2 billion in fiscal Q4 2025 (quarter ended 28 August 2025), an annualised run rate of nearly US$8 billion.
evidence_found: Sanjay Mehrotra: "In fiscal Q4, our HBM revenue grew to nearly $2 billion, implying an annualized run rate of nearly $8 billion." (MarketBeat Micron Q4 FY25 call transcript)
notes: Third-party aggregator transcript (tier 3). Micron's press release (SRC-0097) does not contain this HBM figure; Micron's own prepared remarks would be the tier-1 source.

original_interpretation: Micron said its data center business reached a record 56% of total company revenue in fiscal 2025, with 52% gross margin.
evidence_found: Sanjay Mehrotra: "In fiscal 2025, Micron's data center business reached a record 56% of total company revenue, with gross margins of 52%." (MarketBeat Micron Q4 FY25 call transcript)
notes: Tier-3 aggregator transcript; not in the SRC-0097 press release.

original_interpretation: In September 2025 Micron said it had pricing agreements with almost all customers for the vast majority of its calendar-2026 HBM3E supply and expected to sell out the rest of its 2026 HBM supply in the following months.
evidence_found: Sanjay Mehrotra: "We have pricing agreements with almost all customers for a vast majority of our HBM3E supply in calendar 2026...we expect to conclude agreements to sell out the remainder of our total HBM calendar 2026 supply in the coming months." (MarketBeat Micron Q4 FY25 call transcript)
notes: Dated statement (23 Sep 2025); later Micron updates on 2026 HBM sell-out were not checked. Tier-3 aggregator transcript.

original_interpretation: Micron said its HBM share was on track to be in line with its overall DRAM share in calendar Q3 2025.
evidence_found: Sanjay Mehrotra: "We are pleased to note that our HBM share is on track to grow again and be in line with our overall DRAM share in this calendar Q3." (MarketBeat Micron Q4 FY25 call transcript)
notes: Forward-looking management expectation as of Sep 2025, not a measured share.

original_interpretation: Micron's Cloud Memory Business Unit revenue rose from US$1.45 billion in fiscal Q4 2024 to US$4.54 billion in fiscal Q4 2025, with 59% gross margin.
evidence_found: CMBU table: "Revenue $4,543 $3,386 $1,449" and "Gross margin 59% 58% 49%" for FQ4-25 (ended Aug 28, 2025), FQ3-25, FQ4-24 (ended Aug 29, 2024) (Micron Q4 FY25 press release, GlobeNewswire, 23 Sep 2025)
notes: Values are USD millions (4,543 = US$4.54bn; 1,449 = US$1.45bn). 'fact' typing for a company results release is acceptable; quarterly figures are unaudited.

original_interpretation: Samsung's semiconductor (DS) division reported KRW 27.9 trillion revenue but only KRW 0.4 trillion operating profit in Q2 2025, citing one-off inventory value adjustments and export restrictions related to China.
evidence_found: "The DS Division posted KRW 27.9 trillion in consolidated revenue and KRW 0.4 trillion in operating profit for the second quarter."; profitability hit by "inventory value adjustments in memory and one-off costs related to the impacts of export restrictions related to China in non-memory"; Foundry weakness from "inventory value adjustments that stemmed from US export restrictions on advanced AI chips to China, as well as a continued low utilization rates at mature nodes." (Samsung Q2 2025 results, 31 Jul 2025)
notes: Samsung also cites low foundry utilisation at mature nodes, which the claim omits.

original_interpretation: The AI memory boom did not lift all memory makers equally: in 2025 SK hynix earned record profits on HBM while Samsung's chip division was near break-even in Q2 2025, with the gap attributed to HBM position rather than to DRAM demand as a whole.
evidence_found: Samsung attributes the Q2 2025 DS result to "inventory value adjustments in memory and one-off costs related to the impacts of export restrictions related to China in non-memory" and low foundry utilisation (SRC-0260), while noting it expanded HBM3E sales. SK hynix FY25 record results and HBM revenue more than doubling (SRC-0257).
correction: The contrast (SK hynix record 2025 profit vs Samsung DS KRW 0.4tn operating profit in Q2 2025) is supported. Attributing the gap to HBM position is not what Samsung says: it cites one-off inventory valuation adjustments, China export-control costs and low foundry utilisation. The comparison also sets a full year (SK hynix 2025) against one quarter (Samsung Q2 2025), and a memory-focused company against a division that includes foundry and System LSI.

original_interpretation: Counterpoint Research estimated HBM market shares in 3Q25 of 57% for SK hynix, 22% for Samsung (up from 15% in 2Q25) and 21% for Micron.
evidence_found: "SK hynix remained in first place with a market share of 57% in the third quarter of 2025"; "Samsung's HBM share jumped from 15% in the second quarter to 22% in the third quarter"; "Micron's HBM share was 21% in both quarters" (Mark LaPedus Substack, 24 Dec 2025, citing Counterpoint Research; basis described as HBM sales)
notes: Verified only as reported by a tier-3 blog. Counterpoint's own page (counterpointresearch.com/insights/global-dram-and-hbm-market-share) was opened but its data was not readable; a search summary also mentioned a 56/23/21 split for Q3 2025 from another outlet (not opened), so the exact split is not independently confirmed. Counterpoint's page (updated Sep 2026) carries newer quarters.
